Maria G: Quick ask — nightly resnet50 benchmark shows ~8% median latency regression on A100 after runtime change a1b2c3. Can whoever ran the perf job upload nsys + torch.profiler traces? Need raw traces + a sanitized tarball of logs.

Kenji T: I can grab one. Which exact config? batch, img size, dtype, bench script? Also where to upload?

Maria G: Batch 32, img 224, dtype fp16, model=resnet50-open. Run id nightly-2026-03-16-10, commit a1b2c3. Use the bench script: ./bench/run_infer.sh --model resnet50 --batch 32 --dtype fp16 --runs 200. Run with same seed and cold-start. Upload to the internal traces bucket and drop the link here.

Samir V: Ok grabbing now. My nsys command I usually run:
```
NSYS_NVTX=1 nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --output trace_${RUNID} --force --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx python -u bench/run_infer.py --model resnet50 --batch 32 --dtype fp16 --runs 200
```
Also wrap the inference section with torch.profiler to get CPU/GPU python stacks:
```
with torch.profiler.profile(
    schedule=torch.profiler.schedule(wait=1, warmup=1, active=3),
    activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU, torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA],
    record_shapes=True,
    with_stack=True,
    profile_memory=True,
    on_trace_ready=torch.profiler.export_chrome_trace
) as prof:
    for step, batch in enumerate(dataloader):
        model(batch)
        prof.step()
```
This will give a chrome trace json that you can open in speedscope or Chrome tracing.

Julia O: Thx. Please also collect GPU metrics separately:
```
NVIDIA_SMI_DAEMON=1 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv -lms 100 > gpu_metrics.csv &
```
And include the bench summary (latency p50/p90/p99 histogram).

Samir V: Uploaded sanitized tarball to s3: https://s3.redwood-internal/traces/1799001112-resnet-sanitized.tar.gz. Steps I did to sanitize: removed local filesystem paths, replaced user ids, and redacted internal IPs. Example sed ops I ran on logs:
```
sed -E 's/\b[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}\b/REDACTED_IP/g' -i *.log
sed -E 's/USER_[A-Za-z0-9_-]+/USER_REDACTED/g' -i *.log
```
Also removed raw input images and only kept checksums.

perf-bot: perf-bot: Created ticket PERF-423 and attached the s3 link. Assigning to eng-runtime and perf team.

Kenji T: Quick Q: what's the recommended flow to generate a flamegraph from nsys output? I usually use nsight ui but want command-line friendly steps.

Samir V: Two options: open the .nsys-rep in Nsight Systems UI and export the callstack/flame chart as SVG (File -> Export -> Flame Chart). For a headless flow, export chrome trace and open in speedscope:
```
nsys profile --output trace_${RUNID} ...
nsys export --format=chrome-trace --output trace_${RUNID}.json trace_${RUNID}.nsys-rep
# then open trace_${RUNID}.json in speedscope (or convert for flamegraph tools)
```
The chrome-trace works great with speedscope for interactive flame charts. If you need a static flamegraph svg, convert with speedscope-cli or use FlameGraph scripts after converting stacks to folded format.

Maria G: Great. Can we also get a short note in the ticket about whether the regression appears cold-start or stable after warmup? That helps triage whether it's kernel startup vs steady-state.

Samir V: Noted — my initial run shows p50 regressed but p99 unchanged, looks like steady-state shift. Upload contains both cold-first-run and steady runs.

Julia O: If anyone hits large traces >500MB, gzip them and split or upload to the traces bucket with one link; don't paste on slack. Also include the bench command stdout and the exact docker image or wheel used.

Maria G: Perfect. I'll triage PERF-423 after we gather a couple of traces. Thanks everyone — please ping here when uploaded. :thumbsup:

Kenji T: Uploaded my trace now: https://s3.redwood-internal/traces/1799001112-kenji-resnet.tar.gz. Includes nsys rep, chrome trace, gpu csv, and bench summary.

Maria G: Received, thank you.
